```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(Cohort2Trajectory)
```

Cohort records describe intervals: when a patient was observed and when each
clinical state applied. Cohort2Trajectory turns those records into patient
histories using the same selection and transition rules for every patient.

The target cohort defines each patient's observation period. State cohorts
describe events or conditions within that period. You define their clinical
meaning, choose how to handle overlaps, and request either fixed-length cycles
or continuous intervals. The resulting table can be used for trajectory plots
or state-transition analysis.

This example uses local data, so you do not need a database connection.
For an OMOP database, see [Import cohort data](a02_import.html).

## Supply the cohort intervals

Patient `001` is observed for 14 days. State A covers the first week and
state B covers the second. Patient `002` is observed for ten days and has
no state records.

```{r input}
input <- data.frame(
  subject_id = c("001", "001", "001", "002"),
  cohort_definition_id = c("0", "A", "B", "0"),
  cohort_start_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-01", "2020-01-01", "2020-01-08", "2020-01-01"
  )),
  cohort_end_date = as.Date(c(
    "2020-01-14", "2020-01-07", "2020-01-14", "2020-01-10"
  ))
)
```

`"0"` identifies target-cohort rows. Other values are state labels. Dates include
both endpoints. Keep identifiers as text if leading zeros matter.

## Configure, import and generate

Choose seven-day cycles and put B ahead of A when they overlap. The priority
rule is part of the study settings, even though this example has no overlaps.

```{r run, results='hide', message=FALSE}
studyPath <- tempfile("c2t-getting-started-")
dir.create(studyPath)

study <- cohort2TrajectoryConfiguration(
  studyName = "Example",
  pathToStudy = studyPath,
  useCDM = FALSE,
  trajectoryDataObject = input,
  stateCohortLabels = c("A", "B"),
  stateCohortPriorityOrder = c("B", "A"),
  stateSelectionType = "Priority",
  trajectoryType = "Discrete",
  cycleLength = 7
)
getDataForStudy(studyEnv = study)
trajectories <- createTrajectories(studyEnv = study)
```

## Read the result

```{r result}
knitr::kable(trajectories[c(
  "subject_id", "state_label", "state_start_date", "state_end_date"
)], row.names = FALSE)
```

Patient `002` is still included. Both cycles have the label `OUT OF COHORT`
because no state was supplied. This label marks a cycle with no selected state.
The second cycle ends on January 10, the target-cohort end date.

`START` is the start boundary. `EXIT` is the day after the last cycle and does
not add an observed day. Neither is a clinical state.

The function returns the trajectory table and saves it under
`Example/Data/patientDataDiscrete.csv`. The completed analysis settings are
saved under `Example/Settings/analysisSettings.rds` so the study can be repeated
with fresh input. The returned table also carries its state definitions and
cycle length; use `saveRDS()` to preserve these when saving the table in R.
